question_type: z-score (sample SD) of one year's value within a 5-value series; each value is the printed calendar-year Total row of a different year's end-of-February PDO-1 maturity schedule (two-panel OCR table with garbled year stubs)
decisive_step: For each year Y read the printed 'Total' row of the FIRST calendar-year block of the left panel of the PDO-1 table dated 'Outstanding February 28/29, Y' (March issue of year Y), ignoring the OCR year stub (the 1972 block is labelled 1976, the 1973 Total sits beside a '1978' stub) and not re-summing line items (two OCR defects break the re-sum in 1974 and 1975). Reference: worklog.md Step 4 (treasury_bulletin_1972_03.txt:2098, 1973_03.txt:2370, 1974_03.txt:2237, 1975_03.txt:1987, 1976_03.txt:2007) and Step 3 (March 1976 issue carries two PDO-1 tables, Feb 29 and Jan 31).

a.path_summary: find_tables never hit the 1970s PDO-1 (a[5]-[9], 0 parts even with the full title and --years 1972-1976), so a fell back to rg on the corpus and found the five March-issue tables by their 'Outstanding February 28/29, 197x' subtitles (a[22]-[24]). show_table --long on the 1972 table showed every left-panel row with period '1976' (a[29]); a recognised the side-by-side panel/garbled stub (a[30], a[32]) and switched to sed on the raw lines. It printed each of the five tables raw (a[31], a[41], a[47], a[49], a[51]), took the first block's printed Total each time ('1973 total ... Good'), computed mean/stdev/z in calc (a[43]) and, after one re-sum of the 1972 items disagreed with the printed Total (a[45]-[46]), kept the printed Totals.

tool_use.friction: find_tables 0 hits for the 1970s PDO-1 by title (a[5], a[7], a[9]); officeqa.py search API misuse (a[11] exit 1, a[16]-[20]); show_table --grep 1972 returned 'page rows 0-0 of 0' because the tool's filled period for the 1972 block is '1976' (a[27]); show_table --long labelled all left-panel rows 1976 and paged at 19 of 72 rows (a[29]); printings --row 1972 useless for a one-date snapshot (a[33]); zsh word-splitting bug in a for-loop (a[35]-[37] exit 1)

a.text_use: yes: 'Provenance: ... print the line it comes from' (a[41]-[52], one raw print per table, each followed by 'total ... Good'); 'Compute every final number with calc' (a[43], a[45])

b.path_summary: Same locate path as a: find_tables missed (b[5]-[8]), rg on 'Table PDO-1|Outstanding February' found the five March issues (b[14]). show_table --stitch on the 1972 table looked 'weird' (b[16]-[17]) so b dropped to raw sed/python. Its python filter for rows starting '| 19' or '| Total' (b[23]) printed rows with shifted stubs, and for the 1973 table b decided the left panel 'starts 1973' at the stub-labelled '1977' rows only, summed in its head the amounts of the three OCR-merged rows under that stub (b[28]), and treated the printed 1973 Total row (which carries a '1978' stub) as the 1974 total. That one input was ~40% low; the z-score came out well under half of a's magnitude (error_bin >25pct). The gate fired `grounded` on exactly that input, b searched the corpus for it, found nothing (b[44]), and kept anyway with a prose reason (b[46]).

first_divergence.what_it_did: Assigned the calendar-1973 block by the flattened stub labels instead of by the maturity dates in the Description column; mentally summed only the first three (OCR-merged, 'two securities per cell') rows and used that unprinted number as the 1973 input, skipping the printed Total row two lines below.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: a[41]-[42] and c[30]-[31] printed the raw 1973 table and took the first printed 'Total' row of the left panel as the 1973 value; the reference did the same at worklog Step 4 (1973_03.txt:2370) and re-summed the items only as a check.

b.harness_use: 3 submits, 2 gate rounds, 0 loop notes, no compaction. Round 1 (call 18) showed only `flagged_cells`: the CORRECT 1972 Total on a SHIFT+1 repaired row, with the misleading hint 'printings --row 1976' (period taken from the garbled stub); b re-verified that value and kept (b[42]). `grounded` (the real error: 'calc uses <the hand-summed 1973 input>, a value no tool output showed') also fired in round 1 but was hidden by gate_findings_per_round=1 and shown only in round 2 (call 20); it carried no offer. b's rg found no line with the value (b[44]) yet it kept with a prose reason (b[46]) and round 3 recorded it because gate_rounds_max=2 was used up. Net: the right signal existed, was ranked second, and was dismissable by prose; it did not change the answer.

smallest_change.change: Keep a's provenance sentence verbatim in the v10 AGENTS.md: 'Provenance: use numbers you have seen printed by a tool. Before you rely on a value, print the line it comes from, so the number in your calculation is the number in the source.' Add one clause for block tables: 'For a table with calendar-year blocks, use the block's printed Total row; if the year stub looks wrong, anchor the block by the dates in its Description cells.' Both cells that had the first sentence (a, c) printed each Total line before using it; b, which lacked it, typed a hand-summed value no tool had printed.
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: no - a and c already followed it and were right; the sentence adds one print per value

alternatives.change: Rank `grounded` (a calc input that no tool output ever printed) above `flagged_cells` (a repair flag on a printed cell) so it is the first finding shown, and refuse a `--keep` for `grounded` unless the keep reason cites a file:line whose text contains the value; the harness prints 'No printed line contains <value>; print the line it comes from (rg -n "<value>" <file>) before submitting.' b saw the finding second, ran the rg itself, got nothing, and still kept with prose (b[44]-[46]).
alternatives.why_not_first: It only fires at submit time after the wrong value is already in the calculation and depends on b then re-reading the table correctly; the text guard prevents the ungrounded value up front and was demonstrated by a and c.

alternatives.change: In show_table/printings, when a period stub is a year but the row's Description cell contains a maturity date 'm/d/yy' or a series-year, derive the row period from the description and print it as period '1972 (from description; stub reads 1976)'; also print one line per calendar-year block: 'BLOCK 1973: lines 2362-2370, Total at line 2370'. The 1972 table would then have shown period 1972 (not 1976) on every left-panel row, the --grep 1972 filters at a[27]/c[17] would have matched, the gate's flagged_cells hint would have said --row 1972, and b would have seen the 1973 Total line named explicitly in its first show_table call (b[16]) instead of abandoning the tool for raw dumps.
alternatives.why_not_first: Needs new code in otables.py (description-date anchoring, block detection) and only helps a cell that stays on the tool; b, a and c all abandoned show_table for raw text after the mislabelled output, so the text guard is the cheaper certain fix. Worth doing in v10 because the same mislabel also produced the misleading gate hint.

notes: Tool behaviour that hurt every cell: (1) on two-panel PDO-1 tables show_table fills the left panel's period from the OCR-garbled first stub (a[29], c[21]: all rows '1976'), so --grep <year> filters return nothing (a[27], c[17]) and the model abandons the tool; the same wrong period fed the gate's 'printings --row 1976' hint in b. (2) find_tables does not surface the 1970s PDO-1 at all (a[9] exact title, 0 parts). (3) printings --row <year> on a snapshot table returns unrelated cells (a[33], b[40]). Reference pitfalls confirm re-summing items is unsafe here (OCR digit error in 1974, merged row in 1975) - the printed Total is the value 'as reported'. b's failure came from hand-summing exactly such OCR-merged rows. Mechanism note for v10 controls: gate_findings_per_round=1 hid the decisive `grounded` finding behind a repair flag on a correct cell, and a prose `--keep` dismissed it; the v8 prompt-arm failure on this question (values hidden by 10 KB output truncation) did not recur in v9 because cells read one table per call.
